claims.text: The initial TiVNbTa alloy has a single-phase BCC dendritic microstructure.
A powder-metallurgy route can incorporate fine Y2O3 nanoparticles into the TiVNbTa BCC matrix.
The proposed processing will produce a uniform nanoscale dispersion of Y2O3 particles in the BCC matrix.
Dispersed Y2O3 particles will obstruct dislocation motion in TiVNbTa.
Dispersed Y2O3 particles will suppress grain-boundary sliding at elevated temperature.
Obstructing dislocation motion and grain-boundary sliding will retard high-temperature softening and preserve strength.
The Y2O3 dispersion will remain thermally stable around 1273 K.
At 1273 K, ODS-treated TiVNbTa will have markedly greater mechanical strength than untreated TiVNbTa.
At 1273 K, the ODS-treated alloy's yield strength may increase well above 330 MPa.
At 1273 K, the ODS-treated alloy's compressive strength may increase above 423 MPa.
The ODS-treated alloy will maintain acceptable ductility for the intended heat-transfer application.
Untreated TiVNbTa has a yield strength of about 330 MPa at 1273 K.
Untreated TiVNbTa has a compressive strength of 423 MPa at 1273 K.
The predicted improvement may not extrapolate beyond approximately 1273 K or to substantially different strain rates.

The hypothesis is to be rejected if ODS treatment fails to produce a statistically significant improvement, operationalized as at least a 20% increase in yield and/or compressive strength at 1273 K without significant ductility loss.
